title: Bridge Abutments on Chester Valley Trail (ex Chester Valley Railroad)
description: I walked the Chester Valley Trail yesterday between Contention Lane to Devon Alley Forge Rd.  First time I had ever been in there.    I came upon an old pair of bridge abutments, behind at about where the McDonald’s on Swedesford Rd is.   I took these two photos looking east at about 4 PM.  The abutment on the right (the second, brighter photo) is more elaborate, with wider wing walls and appears to have an ornamental column on the east side, where even today, there is a stone-paved walkway up to it with signs of use. I didn’t go up there to explore. - Jim Brazel

title: Tom Nelson
description:
On South Leopard Road, across from where we lived was Doctor Thomas Nelson, who had a large estate.  They had a son Thomas who was a mothers boy ... and he was not allowed to talk or play with us kids.  He also had a pony, named Major, white, which he would ride down to the road.  We had a tennis court and he would like to come down and try to play .. he was very friendly at that point.  When he got older and got a car he would drive by our house with head in the air and makeout like he never saw us .. speak or wave.  When he got married his wife as also like that.

George Moran, 1987

title: Duffy’s Cut enclosure
description:
This enclosure was built at the purported / believed gravesite of the Irish immigrant laborers who died en masse during the construction of "Duffy’s Cut" on the Philadelphia & Columbia in the early 1830s.
  
It is located on the south side of the ROW, just west of where Sugartown Road formerly crossed the P&C and later the PRR.  There is a PA state marker at King St. & Sugartown Rd. commemorating the tragedy.
 
This enclosure was built in 1909 when Martin Clement of PRR management investigated the site. He later (1935-48) became  president of the PRR.  It is substantially built out of salvaged stone sleeper blocks from the original P&C Railroad. Note the drilled holes for spiking the rail to the block. 

The generally accepted number of fatalities is fifty-seven and recently, human remains have been found.
rights: Owned by the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society

title: Pickering Creek Farm
description:
This "AIRGRAPH" photo taken by Aero Service Group, Philadelphia, has been copied from the collection of Edward Ludwick, Jr. of Gladwyne PA.  It shows the property "Pickering Creek Farm" of his grandfather, George Priestly, on Valley Park Road in Schuylkill Township, looking east towards Valley Forge.

Mr. Ludwick’s father, Edward Ludwick, Sr., had the architect’s commission to perform a modernization of the property in the early 1920s, after his father in law had purchased it.  Mr. Ludwick recalls that extensive modernization and stonework were done on the main house and that the main barn and entrance driveway were also modernized.  His mother, Bessie Priestley Ludwick, remembered the Phoenixville, Valley Forge, and Strafford railway trolley going by in the early 1920s.  The tracks and poles for the trolley line are visible in the bottom of the photo, on the south side of Valley Park Road.

Written by J. Brazel from interview with Edward Ludwick, Jr., 30 December 2014.
